answer: An agent economy can root admission in a trust graph grown from established anchors: each anchor may endorse only a few newcomers per epoch, and every endorsement carries a shrinking share of the endorser’s standing — a ledge of trust that narrows with each hop, so a farm’s thousand heads all hang from one thin plume of borrowed reputation. Endorsers lose standing if a protege is caught faking, and a cedar of deep roots takes seasons to grow, so cloning a thousand identities means a thousand separate slow climbs, each priced in the endorser’s own standing.
